simple.meaning: קְצָת (qᵉtsâth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a termination (literally or figuratively); also (by implication) a portion ; adverbially (with prepositional prefix) after.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 37:8. The surrounding context includes kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קְצָת (H7117) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

majorEvents.evidenceText: The Lord* The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God; † The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים” (Elohim). and he carried them into the land of Shinar to the house of his god. He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.

timeline.evidenceText: one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end. He made the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat at its two ends.
He cast four rings for the four corners of bronze grating, to be places for the poles.
They made shoulder straps for it, joined together. It was joined together at the two ends.
their camels, four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.

The Lord* The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God; † The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים” (Elohim). and he carried them into the land of Shinar to the house of his god. He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
The king appointed for them a daily portion of the king’s dainties, and of the wine which he drank, and that they should be nourished three years; that at its end they should stand before the king.
At the end of ten days, their faces appeared fairer, and they were fatter in flesh, than all the youths who ate of the king’s dainties.
At the end of the days which the king had appointed for bringing them in, the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.

definitions.full: H7117. qetsath קְצָת noun feminine end (Lag BN 10 Ges § 95n ); — construct ׳ק Neh 7:69 (Gi Baer, 7:70 van d. H.) +; suffix קְצָתָם Dan 1:5 ; plural absolute קְצָוֺת Exod 38:5 ; Psa 65:9 ( + perhaps קצוותו Exod 37:8 ; 39:4 Kt. see קָצָה ; Kö ii. 1, 61 derives these plural forms from [ קָ֑צוּ ]); — 1 end , of corners of grating Exod 38:5 (|| קְצוֺתָיו 27:4 ), compare 37:8 ; 39:4 above (all P); ends of earth Psa 65:9 . 2 מִקְצָת (some) from the end of, some of ( מִן 3b ) Neh 7:69 (so Late Hebrew), Dan 1:2 . 3 ׳מִק at the end of a certain time Dan 1:5 , 15 , 18 . II. קצה (√ of following (Ol § 215 h Kö ii. 1, 405 ); compare Arabic decide judicially, decree , †adi ). קְצָת noun feminine end (so Biblical Hebrew (late); ᵑ7 ( Gen 47:2 ); not Syriac; compare Egyptian Aramaic RŠS 361A 4 ); — construct ׳לִק at the end of (months, days) Dan 4:26 ; 4:31 ; ׳מִןקֿ מַלְכוּתָא 2:42 = part of (|| מִנַּהּ v d ; compare Biblical Hebrew קְצָת 2 ).
